name: Communication differences
summary: Communication differences in neurodivergence include variation in timing, reciprocity, inference, speech, language, non-speaking communication and interaction style; some difficulties arise from mismatch between communication partners rather than residing entirely in one person.

includes: Differences in social communication style, timing and interpretation.
Interaction between autistic and non-autistic communication styles.
Spoken, written and augmentative communication needs.
excludes: Assuming communication difficulty means lack of interest, empathy or understanding.
Treating all autistic communication differences as identical.
Reducing all communication barriers to the double-empathy account.

claims.text: Studies of autistic and non-autistic interaction show that communication and rapport can depend on the match between partners' neurotypes, supporting an interactional component rather than a purely one-sided deficit account.

sources.citation: Crompton CJ et al. Neurotype-Matching, but Not Being Autistic, Influences Self and Observer Ratings of Interpersonal Rapport. Frontiers in Psychology. 2020;11:586171.

uncertainties.question: Which communication barriers are best explained by neurotype mismatch, language processing, anxiety, sensory context, speech access or other factors?
uncertainties.why_it_matters: The same outward communication difficulty can arise for different reasons and may require different supports.
what_would_reduce_it: Replicated interaction studies across more diverse communication modes and support needs.
Research including non-speaking people and AAC users rather than treating speech as the default.

perspectives.summary: Communication success is partly relational and contextual; this challenges one-sided deficit assumptions without denying individual communication impairments or support needs.

relations.note: Social-communication differences are central to autism descriptions, but interaction context changes how difficulty appears.
Language impairment and autistic social-communication differences can overlap in everyday impact without being identical.
Describing internal emotion can be one communication challenge for some people, but alexithymia is neither necessary nor sufficient for broader communication difference.

questions: Can written communication, processing time or AAC reduce the interaction barrier?
Does assessment distinguish speech, language, social interaction and communication access?

provenance.method: Evidence-bounded content expansion for v0.9. Primary research or authoritative source checked on 2026-08-28; claims are deliberately narrower than the source and uncertainty remains explicit.
